coded_because: USART_TDR's write must also trigger TXE-clear/TC-recompute and hand the byte to the TX net -- not just store (fails 'every write only stores'). Separately, USART_CR1 and USART_ISR are SVD-modelled as two full ALTERNATE register definitions at the same offset (0x00 and 0x1C respectively) depending on the live value of CR1.FIFOEN, so a fixed field list cannot describe a read at those offsets without a runtime branch (fails 'every read is a pure function of stored state' under the doc's own field-list-is-fixed reading of that clause). Per the doc's whole-peripheral granularity ruling (SS1.8), the FIFO-occupancy-derived-fields ruling (SS1, third bullet under 'Two rulings'), and its explicit UART worked example ('UART data and FIFO flags... an RX read pops a FIFO'), the entire peripheral routes to coded:, not just TDR/CR1/ISR.
source: RM0490 Rev 6 Chapter 26 (USART); STM32C031.svd peripheral USART2 (derivedFrom=USART1, identical layout)
verified: 2026-08-24. Same two-chain split as peripherals.stm32c0.rcc.json's reference case. (1) Bits/offsets: mechanically drafted from SVD, including the CR1/ISR alternate-register split at FIFOEN=0/1 (structural fact about the SVD's own modelling, not a reset-value question). (2) Reset values: SVD-ONLY for CR1=0x0, BRR=0x0, and ISR=0x008000C0 -- ISR's non-zero reset word was hand-decoded bit-by-bit (see usart_isr_reset below) to confirm it's internally self-consistent with its own field list, but no independent RM sentence or CMSIS default was cross-checked against it the way RCC_CR's HSIDIV was; recorded as the weaker corroboration tier, same honesty standard as the GPIO contract. Spin behaviour (which flag HAL_UART_Transmit actually waits on) traced to stm32c0xx_hal_uart.c:3407 (UART_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout, the shared HAL_GetTick-gated wait helper) -- did not individually trace every call site's Flag argument this session, so which exact bit (TXE vs TC) gates which specific HAL call is UNVERIFIED beyond confirming the wait mechanism exists and is HAL_GetTick-timed like every other HAL spin in this drop.
board_choice: USART2, not USART1 -- nucleo-c031c6-bsp: COM1_UART=USART2, TX=PA2/AF1, RX=PA3/AF1, routed to the onboard ST-LINK VCP. This is what printf() over the Nucleo's USB-serial port actually goes through on this specific board.

design_notes_for_the_python_class.cr1_fifoen_mux: Bit 29 (FIFOEN, reset=0) selects between two live meanings for several other bits at the SAME offset. FIFOEN=0 (classic, what stock HAL_UART_Init leaves it at -- FIFO mode is opt-in via HAL_UARTEx_* on this family): CR1 bit7=TXEIE/bit5=RXNEIE, ISR bit7=TXE/bit5=RXNE/bit6=TC. FIFOEN=1: CR1 bit7=TXFNFIE/bit5=RXFNEIE, ISR bit7=TXFNF/bit5=RXFNE/bit23=TXFE/bit24=RXFF/bit26=RXFT/bit27=TXFT. 'This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE=0)' per its own SVD text. Recommend implementing only the classic/FIFOEN=0 variant first (this repo's 'thin path first' build-order rule) since that's what a stock printf-over-VCP firmware actually exercises; treat FIFOEN=1 as a documented gap.
design_notes_for_the_python_class.usart_isr_reset: 0x008000C0 -- VERIFIED by exact bit decode: bits {23,7,6} set. Bit6=TC=1, bit7=TXE(classic)/TXFNF(FIFO)=1, bit23=reserved(classic)/TXFE(FIFO)=1. Both variants report 'transmit path empty/ready' immediately at reset, before UE/TE are even set -- trivially true since no write to TDR has happened yet.
design_notes_for_the_python_class.tdr_write_behaviour: Writing USART_TDR (offset 0x28) should: store the byte, clear TXE (classic) for the duration modelled, hand the byte to whatever is listening on the TX net (websocket/virtual console), and set TC once the (possibly zero-length, for an instant-transmit MVP) byte time has elapsed. Zero simulated transmit latency (TXE/TC both flip back to 1 on the very next read after a TDR write) is a legitimate first-pass choice matching a 'working printf' rather than 'cycle-accurate baud-rate-timed UART' goal -- flagged as the natural next increment once a byte-time counter is wanted, not built now.
design_notes_for_the_python_class.brr_and_baud: USART_BRR (offset 0x0C, plain data-shaped rw, NOT part of this contract's coded core -- could live in a small regmap sidecar if the engine wants config fields split from the coded I/O fields, but is grouped here for now since it's meaningless without the peripheral it configures). HAL_UART_Init computes USARTDIV = PCLK/baud from RCC_CFGR.PPRE's resulting PCLK -- wrong PPRE silently produces a garbage baud rate (printf outputs noise), not a hang, so this is a correctness dependency worth a conformance fixture even though nothing spins on it.
design_notes_for_the_python_class.rcc_dependency: Must consult RCC.APBENR1.USART2EN (see peripherals.stm32c0.rcc.json) the same way GPIO must consult IOPENR -- writes should store but produce no observable TX-net effect if the clock is gated.
